title: The Town Hall concert of 1967
summary: A caller from Town Hall proposed a concert; she asked Cliff to assemble the group.

but I think the next stage you told me of coming out of your retirement was the Town Hall Concert you did in 1967.
I got a call from a man who, evidently he worked with Town Hall. I supposed -- the way we figured it out, he had access to a little time at Town Hall.
So, he contacted me and wanted to know if I would want to do a concert, which I would have to more or less promote myself.
They would print the tickets and we would invite our friends. And, I guess, split the proceeds.

So, I spoke to Cliff and asked him if he could get the group together which he said yeah. And we sent out a lot of invitations to his friends and my friends. And we did this concert at Town Hall, with Tony Parenti on clarinet; Max Kaminsky on trumpet; Marshall Brown on trombone; Sonny Greer on

drums; and Cliff on piano.

This was the one and only time that
Cliff and I ever worked together, because we -- I
wanted to -- for us to work together, but it just
didn't come off.

Cliff was not interested for some
reason or other. I guess it's back to the same
thing when you're a solo pianist, you don't want
to be -- you want to accompany somebody but you
don't want to be known as somebody's accompanist.

So that was another situation where
we couldn't team up.

So anyway, the concert was artistically
a success. We didn't draw that many people because
I had been away for a long time, and I don't supposed
there were that many people who knew that I was
still around.

But it was a very good concert. And
John Wilson and he reviewed it. And he -- in fact,
his review was titled "Maxine Sullivan Evokes The
Swing Era." That was 1967.
